increments.title: Coverage inventory script with covered-cells diff and worklist
increments.goal: A static coverage inventory (`scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js`) that parses the whole fixture corpus, extracts every occurring rule-construct combination cell, diffs it against a machine-readable record of covered cells, and writes the uncovered cells to `docs/testing/worklist.json` — so the two skills of the later increments have a mechanical source of truth to work from.
criteria: `scripts/evaluator-coverage-inventory.js` exists and parses every `.cat`/`.gst` file of both fixture sets (`src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/` and `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/`) statically, without rosters and without running the evaluator.

It records every occurring combination cell with occurrence count and file locations along these axes: constraint field-class x scope x flags (`shared`, `includeChildSelections`, `includeChildForces`, `percentValue`); condition type x scope x field-class; repeat attributes; modifier type x target-field-class; and the nesting constructs (`conditionGroup` types including `not`, `modifierGroups`, nested `repeats`).
The record of covered cells is machine-readable and the script diffs the inventory against it automatically; no human or agent has to read `docs/testing/constraint-matrix.md` inside the loop.
The uncovered cells are written to `docs/testing/worklist.json`.
The script exits non-zero when the worklist is non-empty and zero when every occurring cell is covered.
The cell extraction is covered by unit tests, and they pass.

increments.title: Invert the constraint-explorer skill to data-first
increments.goal: `.claude/skills/evaluator-constraint-explorer/SKILL.md` rewritten so the explorer starts from the inventory's worklist instead of from engine-code hypotheses, delegates scenario authorship black-box, and treats red scenarios as pinned implementation work rather than deleting them.
criteria: The rewritten skill works data-first: run the inventory script, take the next uncovered cell from `docs/testing/worklist.json`, delegate the scenario for that cell to the `e2e-testcase-author` subagent, then run the evaluator tests (`npx vitest run src/evaluator`).
A green scenario is kept and its cell marked covered in the same commit.
A red scenario stays in place as a pinned gap and is recorded as implementation work for phase B.
Changing a scenario's expectations to make the engine pass is forbidden by the skill text.

A cell whose intended semantics cannot be derived from the catalog data, the BSData wiki or the XSD is parked: the open question goes into the campaign state and the loop continues with the next cell.
The engine-code hypothesis search remains documented as a secondary mode for semantics bugs inside already-covered cells.

increments.title: Campaign driver skill evaluator-closure-loop
increments.goal: A user-invocable skill `evaluator-closure-loop` under `.claude/skills/` that alternates the data-first search (phase A) with implementation rounds (phase B), keeps all campaign state on disk, re-arms itself with `send_later` until the termination criterion holds, and reports parked questions to the human.
criteria: A user-invocable skill `evaluator-closure-loop` exists under `.claude/skills/` that runs the campaign unattended.

It alternates phase A (the inverted explorer working through the worklist) with phase B (run `uroboros:agile-loop` on a campaign issue whose task list is the current set of red scenarios), and re-runs phase A after every phase B round.
It terminates when the worklist is empty, every evaluator E2E scenario is green, and no parked question is open.
At the end of every unfinished run it re-arms the loop with `send_later` about one hour ahead, and stops re-arming once the termination criterion holds.
Each run is capped at a fixed number of cells, and a cell is parked after two failed implementation rounds instead of being retried again.
All campaign state lives in files (worklist, parked questions, campaign issue) so a fresh session resumes from disk alone.
Parked questions are reported to the human at the end of a run, and their recorded answers are folded back in before the parked cells are retried.

steps.label: decompose

return.summary: Cut the issue into three increments mirroring its three acceptance-criteria sections one-to-one: (1) the coverage inventory script with covered-cells diff and worklist, (2) the data-first rewrite of the constraint-explorer skill, (3) the evaluator-closure-loop campaign driver skill. Every criterion of the issue lands in exactly one increment: all of section 1 in inc-1, section 2 in inc-2, section 3 in inc-3. The inventory script comes first because it is the load-bearing risk — the cell taxonomy and the machine-readable covered-cells diff are what both skills consume, and the shape of the covered-cells record (dedicated file vs. derivation from the existing scenario.json manifests) is a code decision the inc-1 researcher answers before the skills depend on it. I rejected a finer cut of section 1 (extraction vs. diff/worklist) because the half without the diff delivers nothing reviewable on its own, and a merge of sections 2 and 3 because the explorer skill is independently testable against the worklist while the driver only orchestrates it. Codemap: seven entries — the new script and its test under scripts/, worklist.json and the covered-cells record plus a stale self-description in constraint-matrix.md under docs/testing/, the rewritten explorer SKILL.md, and the new closure-loop SKILL.md.
